attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his Substack post. The NYT scoop and the tweets he quotes are separate from the claim.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps the 'if sued' antecedent and both firm 'will' predictions: Exhibit One and high punitive damages. Reading 'Exhibit One' as key evidence is a fair paraphrase. No deadline was stated.

contract.note: Reading 'Exhibit One' figuratively as central evidence and 'high' as a substantial, non-nominal award is the ordinary reading. It neither stretches nor shrinks the claim. Counting Montana's general damages request as meeting the condition is a generous reading, but it does not change the result. Pending cases cannot count as failure.

evidence.note: LASST's complaint of Sept 29 asks only for injunctions and fees, with no damages. That falls outside the damages-litigation condition, and it says nothing about the outcome.

Montana's complaint of Oct 14 includes an agent-hacking count and asks for damages. At most it shows the antecedent was met. It is not evidence of an evidentiary ruling or a punitive award, so it is context for the outcome.
Dated Oct 16 legal analysis. It confirms Montana's filing and says none of the allegations have been adjudicated, so no outcome yet.

reviews.rationale: This firm conditional forecast has no deadline. Even if Montana's suit meets the antecedent, no completed proceeding, evidentiary ruling or punitive award existed by Oct 28, 2026. Montana's case was still unadjudicated. The early-resolution rule is not met, and pending cases are not failure. The evidence does not settle the outcome.
